title: Deterministic single-photon sources in hexagonal boron nitride with electron-dose-tuned purity and reversible thermal quenching
authors: Amrita Majumder, Janhavi Khunte, Ikshvaku Shyam, Rohit Kumar, and Anshuman Kumar
abstract: Electron-beam irradiation is an established route to create site-controlled, room-temperature single-photon emitters (SPEs) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), but two aspects remain underexplored: how the electron dose governs the properties of the resulting single emitters, and how the emission behaves when the host is heated above room temperature. Here, we create emitters deterministically with a focused electron beam and confirm single-photon emission across three independent flakes, with $g^{(2)}(0)=0.09$, $0.12$, and $0.16$. We map the single-emitter response (yield, spectrum, lifetime, and photon purity) as a function of electron dose, identifying an optimal window for high-purity single emitters. Consistent with recent cryogenic studies, we assign the bright room-temperature feature near 575 n to the phonon sideband (PSB) of a green--yellow emitter whose zero-phonon line (ZPL) lies near 548 nm. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence measured in situ under real-time from room temperature to 300 degrees C reveals a thermal quenching that is fully reversible upon cooling, in contrast to the irreversible annealing-induced degradation reported elsewhere, indicating that transient heating does not permanently damage the centers. These results add quantitative dose control and above-room-temperature operation to the toolbox for deterministic hBN quantum-light sources.
summary: The authors report on the deterministic creation and characterization of single-photon emitters in hexagonal boron nitride ($	ext{hBN}$) using controlled electron irradiation. They establish a dose window that maximizes emitter purity ($g^{(2)}(0) \ll 1$) while also demonstrating remarkable thermal robustness, with functionality maintained up to $300^\circ	ext{C}$. This work advances the field by providing quantitative control over both the creation process and operational temperature range for quantum light sources.
main_problem: The study aims to systematically investigate how electron dose controls the properties of single-photon emitters (SPEs) in hexagonal boron nitride ($	ext{hBN}$), and to characterize their emission behavior above room temperature.
main_result: High-purity SPEs are deterministically created via controlled electron irradiation, exhibiting robust performance with reversible thermal quenching up to $300^\circ	ext{C}$. The purity is confirmed by low second-order correlation values ($g^{(2)}(0) \le 0.16$).
method: The researchers used localized electron-beam irradiation coupled with photoluminescence microscopy, time-resolved measurements, and Hanbury-Brown and Twiss interferometry to characterize the emitters.
model_or_system: The physical platform is single-photon emitters embedded in hexagonal boron nitride ($	ext{hBN}$), which are activated deterministically using a focused electron beam. The system's performance is mapped against the accumulated electron dose and temperature.
key_observables: Second-order autocorrelation function ($g^{(2)}(0)$), spectral purity (ZPL vs. PSB assignment), emission yield, lifetime ($	au$), Signal-to-Background Ratio ($	ext{SBR}$), and photoluminescence intensity as a function of temperature.
important_parameters: Electron dose (controlled by irradiation time), Temperature ($300^\circ	ext{C}$ maximum), $g^{(2)}(0)$ values ($\sim 0.09$ to $0.16$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the observed spectral features and quantum statistics are dominated by the localized emitter, rather than background or non-radiative processes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate PL maps showing dose dependence (Fig. 2a), spectral evolution vs. dose (Fig. 2b), lifetime/SBR dependence on dose (Figs. 2c/d), and confirmation of high purity across different flake thicknesses (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper systematically details the methodology for dose-controlled emitter creation, presents quantitative data mapping performance metrics (purity, spectrum) against electron dose, confirms spectral assignments (PSB/ZPL), and finally demonstrates thermal stability up to $300^\circ	ext{C}$.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial experimental demonstration of scalable, high-performance quantum light sources operating at ambient temperatures, directly relevant for developing practical photonic quantum technologies.
